author_or_org: Abbas Raza Ali, Muhammad Ajmal Siddiqui, Moona Zahid

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Most enterprise GenAI initiatives fail to show a measurable business effect, and a large fraction of agentic projects are expected to be cancelled.
claims.quote: Frontier language models now produce professional deliverables that expert graders judge to match human work on a substantial share of economically valuable tasks, yet most enterprise GenAI initiatives fail to show a measurable business effect and a large fraction of agentic projects are expected to be cancelled.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The authors frame enterprise GenAI deployment as a measurement problem: public benchmarks ask what models can do, while deployment decisions require assessing whether a workflow is fit, reliable, safe, and worth scaling under local data and controls.
claims.quote: We argue that this is substantially a measurement problem: public benchmarks answer "what can the model do?", whereas a deployment decision requires "is this workflow fit, reliable, safe and worth scaling - here, on our data, under our controls?".

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: EnterpriseVal specifies a use case and a frozen socio-technical configuration under test consisting of model, prompts, retrieval, tools, guardrails, and human oversight, with autonomy level and consequence tier jointly setting required evaluation intensity; it also includes a metric catalogue covering fidelity, utility, efficiency, reliability, assurance, and oversight, plus a threshold gate mapping metric vectors to REJECT/CONDITIONAL/SCALE decisions.
claims.quote: It comprises (i) a formal specification of the use case and of the frozen socio-technical configuration under test, model, prompts, retrieval, tools, guardrails and human oversight, with an autonomy level and consequence tier that jointly set the required evaluation intensity; (ii) a metric catalogue spanning fidelity, utility, efficiency, reliability, assurance and oversight; (iii) a grading protocol that scales blinded expert judgement with calibrated LLM-as-judge scoring through prediction-powered inference; (iv) a two-tier threshold gate, stated as an executable algorithm, that maps metric vectors with confidence bounds to REJECT/CONDITIONAL/SCALE decisions; and (v) a value-and-risk model in which the reviewer catch rate is a measured parameter.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The paper reports a pilot across three workflows in a global bank.
claims.quote: We report a pilot across three workflows in a global bank.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: In the bank pilot, credit-memo drafting achieved 88% human-graded citation precision and 1.6% hallucination rate for the best model against gates of 70% and 5%; in procedure transformation, analyst refinement effort fell from an estimated 27.4 hours to 2.9 hours per document.
claims.quote: In credit-memo drafting, human-graded citation precision reached 88% and hallucination rate 1.6% for the best model against gates of 70% and 5%; in procedure transformation, analyst refinement effort fell from an estimated 27.4 to 2.9 hours per document.
